subject: SLA measurement: RFP questionnaire — evidence & sampling clarifications
messages:

Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: SLA questionnaire — Redwood Inference

Hi Logan,

Thanks for confirming you received the RFP. We've attached the SLA questionnaire spreadsheet (see attachment) and a short list of clarifying questions so we can evaluate measurement and crediting mechanics across vendors. Relevant items we need answered for scoring:

- Precise definition of "availability" (probe vs. customer traffic), measurement cadence, sample sizes.
- Latency percentiles to be reported (p50/p95/p99), whether these are end-to-end, server-only, or exclude queued requests.
- How multi-region failover is accounted for (region weighting, partial-region credits).
- Service credit formula and the timeline for customer claim validation.
- Evidence types you can provide (raw telemetry, query ids, probe traces, audit logs) and retention windows.

Deadline for the RFP is COB 2026-11-10. If you can send an initial protocol and an evidence checklist by 2026-11-04 we'll include you in the initial short-list. Also note we may ask for a short workshop to review sampling assumptions.

Attachment: acme_rfp_sla_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Elena
Procurement Lead — Acme Corporation

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. We'll assemble a focused response that covers definitions, measurement methodology, sample sizes, and the proposed crediting formula. Quick clarifications so our reply maps exactly to your scoring matrix:

2) For latency, do you want client-perceived end-to-end (including network) percentiles, or service-reported server processing percentiles?
3) Any constraints on retaining raw telemetry outside of our standard 90/365 windows for evidence submission?

I've looped in Karthik (observability/telemetry) to draft the measurement spec and Kimberly (contracts/SLA policy) to confirm crediting/legal timelines. From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RFP: SLA questionnaire — telemetry questions

Logan / Kimberly —

Forwarding Elena's thread. Below are the telemetry items I think we should include in the protocol; please flag anything legal/contract that will need different wording. Draft notes:

- Availability definition: 1-minute resolution evaluation of control-plane and data-plane endpoints. Availability = 1 - (#failed_successful_health_checks / #expected_probes) per region.
- Probe types:
  * Synthetic "agent" probes from 3 AZs per region at 60s cadence for control-plane health.
  * Passive sampling of production request traces: rolling 5% sample up to 10k requests/hour for p50/p95/p99 compute.
- Latency: measure both server-processing (time between request received and response sent) and end-to-end (client-to-server-to-client) where customer telemetry is available. For scoring, report both; acceptance threshold will be end-to-end p95.
- Measurement windows: 5-minute sliding windows for incident detection; 30-day aggregated SLO window for monthly calculations.
- Bursts & warmup: ignore the first 5 minutes after deployment/scale events for sampling.

Attachments I can prepare: synthetic_probe_config.yaml (probe specs), query_examples.sql (telemetry queries), and an export template for timestamps and request_ids.

Kimberly, please confirm whether Acme's scoring requires credits to be paid as a percentage of monthly committed fees or as dollar-for-dollar refunds, and what standard notice/claim window we should propose.

-Karthik
Senior Observability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: SLA questionnaire — crediting and evidence guidance

Team —

I've pulled together a concise, customer-facing description we can include in the RFP response. Key points to include (language is intentionally non-legal but maps to contract terms):

1) Availability & measurement
- Primary definition: Availability is measured per-region as the percentage of successful end-to-end requests observed (or synthetic probe successes when customer telemetry is not available), sampled at 1-minute granularity and aggregated into 5-minute sliding windows for incident detection.
- SLO calculation: For the billing month, we compute the weighted average of per-region availability over a 30-day window; weighting is proportional to customer-configured traffic distribution per region.

2) Latency
- We report p50/p95/p99 for both server-processing time and end-to-end where customer-side traces are available.
- For SLO evaluation, the primary metric is end-to-end p95 measured on sampled production traffic. Server-only p95 is provided as diagnostic telemetry.
- We exclude queued or throttled requests from percentile calculations; these are counted toward availability if they ultimately fail.

3) Service credit formula (example)
- If ObservedAvailability < CommittedAvailability then CreditPercentage = min(1.0, (CommittedAvailability - ObservedAvailability) / (1 - CommittedAvailability)).
- Calculated credit = CreditPercentage * MonthlyCommittedFee.
- Example: CommittedAvailability = 99.95%. If observed = 99.70% then CreditPercentage = (0.9995 - 0.9970) / (0.0005) = 5x => capped at 1.0 -> 100% credit of monthly committed fee (we can propose a cap if you prefer partial credit tiers).

4) Evidence and validation
- We can provide: raw probe logs (timestamps, probe ids, region/AZ), sampled request traces (request_id, start/end timestamps, routing metadata), control-plane telemetry, autoscaling events, and a sanitized CSV export suitable for audit.
- Standard retention for evidence exports is 90 days for high-fidelity raw telemetry; we can extend to 365 days under enterprise contracts with minimal additional cost.
- For any disputed incident, we require the customer to provide a claim within 30 days of the end of the billing month to initiate validation. Validation typically completes within 10 business days after claim submission.

5) Multi-region & failover handling
- Availability is region-weighted. If traffic is automatically routed to a healthy region during an outage, we will show the region-level availability and the cross-region failover timeline; credits are attributed to the region that served the traffic in the impacted window.

6) Sampling & statistical confidence
- To avoid small-sample noise we enforce a minimum sample threshold: at least 1,000 successful samples per region per 24-hr period for percentile calculations. If samples < threshold, we fall back to synthetic probes for SLO calculation and clearly annotate this in the evidence package.

7) Artifacts we'll deliver with a claim
- Evidence Collection Binder (PDF) listing query ids, probe ids, and the sequence of validation steps.
- Exported telemetry CSV with request_id, timestamps (ISO8601), region, az, status, latency_ms.
- Synthetic probe config and raw probe logs.

Related: I've uploaded a draft protocol and evidence checklist to Drive (link below) and added the HubSpot deal id so CS/Legal can track. If Acme wants a different credit formula (tiered caps, pro-rated credits), we can propose alternate language in the SOW.

Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cREDWOOD-SLA-PROTOCOL
HubSpot: HUBSPOT-123456

-Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Contracts & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Elena —

Appreciate the quick turn. Attached are the items we discussed: the formal "SLA Measurement Protocol" (PDF), an "Evidence Collection Binder" checklist, and the synthetic probe config for reproducibility. Highlights for your reviewers:

- Availability measured at 1-minute granularity, aggregated into 5-minute sliding windows; 30-day SLO window for monthly credit calculations.
- Latency reporting includes both server-processing and end-to-end percentiles; primary SLO uses end-to-end p95 on sampled production traffic.
- Credit calculation example and proposed cap options are in section 4 of the protocol; we are open to a tiered credit approach if Acme prefers partial credits instead of a hard cap.
- Evidence we provide: raw probe logs, sampled request traces (request_id + timestamps), control-plane audit logs. Default export retention 90 days; can extend to 365 days under enterprise commitments.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Acme wants end-to-end percentiles only or both end-to-end + server-only for scoring.
2) Let us know if you want the workshop; we have availability next Tue/Wed (Nov 9–10) for a 45-minute technical deep-dive.
3) We can add optional contract language for extended retention and an alternate crediting formula in the draft SOW.

Attachments: redwood_sla_measurement_protocol.pdf (formal protocol), evidence_collection_checklist.pdf, synthetic_probe_config.yaml

Best regards,
